agency: Department of Housing and Urban Development
summary: HUD directed the reader to pages 8 and 9 of the final statement for water supply and sanitary waste systems, and noted that the final statement addresses controlled storm runoffs at Kalamazoo and Macon, concluding that the quantity of hydrocarbons and other pollutants discharged into the soil for percolation filtration is small enough for the procedure to be effective.
text: Response: See final statement, pages 8 and 9, for water supply and sanitary waste systems. Final statement addresses the problem of controlled storm runoffs at Kalamazoo and Macon; it is felt that the quantity of hydro-carbons and other pollutants found on the paved areas and discharged into the soil for percolation filtration is small enough for this procedure to be effective.
opening_anchor: Response: See final statement, pages 8 and 9, for water supply and sanitary waste systems.
closing_anchor: it is felt that the quantity of hydro-carbons and other pollutants found on the paved areas and discharged into the soil for percolation filtration is small enough for this procedure to be effective.
